use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: All C² JUs that initiate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic decorrelation capability.

scope_contract.goal_statement: All C² JUs that initiate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic decorrelation capability.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: A C2 JU initiates real-time air or surface tracks and publishes them, applying automatic decorrelation so that each published track is distinct and not redundantly represented.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The C2 JU has real-time air or surface track data ready to be initiated and published.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The initiated real-time tracks are published with automatic decorrelation applied, satisfying the decorrelation requirement for real-time track publication.
in_scope_actions: Automatically decorrelating initiated tracks during publication
excluded_adjacent_actions: Common tracking (sharing a common track number and shifting R² between C² JUs)
Post-publication track consumption or downstream track management

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU must be in Active status, whether initially achieved or after returning from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
The C2 JU must be capable of assuming R² for air, surface, or land tracks.
The C2 JU must have an automatic decorrelation capability.
When a C² JU receives J2 or J3 messages on a common local track, automatic decorrelation tests shall be performed for that track.
The C2 JU completes sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration before transmitting air or surface tracks.
The C2 JU waits the minimum 12 seconds before reporting the air or surface track.
Upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on a common local track (TN A), the C2 JU performs automatic decorrelation tests for that track.

The C2 JU determines that the decorrelation criterion is satisfied because the remote track has fallen outside a distance of 1.5 times the maximum correlation distance on two consecutive remote track reports.

The C2 JU automatically tests the local track once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks) by comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
Because the automatic correlation test fails, the C2 JU assigns a new track number (TN B) to the local track.
The C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report using locally held data and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message with an initial ID of Pending.

Diverges from Step 5. If an operator action has been taken that selectively released a new local track for reporting, the C2 JU transmits that track regardless of the results of correlation testing, rather than relying on the automatic correlation test result as the basis for publication.

Diverges from Step 5. If local/remote data held indicates that two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference constituting a conflict, the C2 JU does not automatically correlate them; instead, the ID differences are presented to operators for evaluation and may require voice coordination for final resolution.
Diverges from Step 5. If the two tracks have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current, the C2 JU does not automatically correlate them.
Diverges from Step 5. If both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data, the C2 JU does not automatically correlate them.

Diverges from Step 6. If TN A is controlled by own unit (subject of a J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message), the C2 JU does not automatically decorrelate; if the operator manually decorrelates, the C2 JU alerts the operator to report termination of control on TN A if appropriate, and reports commencement of control of TN B using J10.5 only if initiated by operator action.

Diverges from Step 6. If TN A has been paired by own unit (subject of a J10.6 message), the C2 JU decorrelates and alerts the operator as a cue to terminate the pairing on TN A and initiate the pairing on TN B if appropriate.

Diverges from Step 6. Instead of proceeding directly with automatic decorrelation and TN B assignment, the C2 JU may perform manual decorrelation, or may require manual confirmation of automatic decorrelations.

Diverges from main flow Step 1. If the operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert (including when a JU without R² receives a J3 or J7.5 (ACT=1) message with remote IFF/SIF data differing from locally held data and must respond per Table 4.7-5), the operator has these manual resolution actions: update local data or verify automatic inputs; initiate J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear IFF/SIF or J7.5 (ACT=1) IFF/SIF Difference Report (any mode); change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; decorrelate local data from remote data, causing assignment of a new track number to local data; and clear the operator alert.

Diverges from main flow Step 5. If the Strength field of either track is set to a value greater than 1, the C2 JU shall not automatically correlate the tracks; this restriction does not apply if either track has its Strength field set to 'No Statement'. Exit: automatic correlation is not performed; continuation is not specified by the evidence.

Diverges from main flow Step 5. If a J7.2 correlation request is received with RV field set to value 3, the C2 JU shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless a restriction applies: the two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; one track is simulated and the other is live; or both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks. Exit: when a restriction applies, the requested correlation is rejected; continuation after rejection is not specified by the evidence.

Diverges from main flow Step 5. If the Retained TN and the Dropped TN decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the correlation shall be rejected. Exit: the correlation is rejected; continuation is not specified by the evidence.

Diverges from main flow Step 5. If a correlation request is rejected for manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination. Exit: the operator alert is provided; continuation is not specified by the evidence.

missing_aspects: Post-resolution continuation after IFF/SIF conflict alert is cleared is not documented.
Post-block continuation after the Strength-field restriction prevents automatic correlation is not documented.
Post-rejection continuation after a correlation request is rejected is not documented.
Explicit evidence describing the exit state or continuation behavior after the operator alert is cleared.

claims.content: The original local track (TN A) has been established as a remote track by the successful decorrelation execution.
The local track has been assigned a new Track Number (TN B) and is reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message with an initial ID of Pending.

The post-resolution continuation after the alert is cleared is undocumented.

inconsistency_hints: The trigger and main flow depend on the C2 JU executing automatic decorrelation to resolve dual designation, but the Preconditions only state Active status and ability to assume R². They do not state that the C2 JU has an automatic decorrelation capability, which is required by the goal and exercised throughout the main flow.

The trigger (EC-TR-001) describes a correlation/dual-designation event: two tracks eligible for correlation require action to resolve dual designation. The main flow and postconditions, however, implement automatic decorrelation of a previously common local track (TN A) after receiving J2/J3 messages, with the decorrelation criterion satisfied when the remote track falls outside 1.5x the maximum correlation distance. Step 1 is only a generic pre-publication check; the concrete flow that leads to the postconditions restarts at step 3 with a new incoming-message event. This is a scenario restart, not a continuation.
